title: General characterization of parallel random-walk cover time
formal: Editorial computational variant: does there exist a deterministic algorithm which, given a connected simple graph \(G\) and an integer \(k\ge1\), outputs a positive rational \(F(G,k)\) in time polynomial in \(|V(G)|+k\), with absolute constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) such that \[cF(G,k)\le t_{\mathrm{cov}}^{(k)}(G)\le CF(G,k)\] for every input? The parallel cover time uses the worst starting tuple and independent lazy walks defined below.
definitions:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite simple connected undirected unweighted graph with \(|V|=n\ge2\). For each walk, at each integer time, stay at the current vertex with probability \(1/2\); otherwise move to a uniformly chosen neighbor. All walk choices are independent, conditional on their positions. The initial tuple \((v_1,\ldots,v_k)\) is deterministic and may contain repetitions. It is chosen before the trajectories are sampled.

All walks take one step simultaneously. Let \[\tau_{\mathrm{cov}}^{(k)}=\min\{t\in\mathbb N_0:\{X_s^{(i)}:1\le i\le k,\ 0\le s\le t\}=V\}.\] Starting vertices already count as visited. The cost is the number of parallel rounds, not the total number \(kt\) of single-walk steps. The expectation is over the trajectories for a fixed initial tuple, and the maximum is taken after these expectations. It is not the expected maximum over start-dependent realizations.

The selected worst-case convention allows all tuples in \(V^k\), rather than requiring all walkers to share one initial vertex. Stationary initialization is a different quantity: each start is sampled independently with probability \(\pi(v)=\deg(v)/(2|E|)\). Both quantities appear in the source and must not be interchanged. The main question allows every positive integer \(k\); bounds stated only for \(k\le n\) are restricted results.

The graph is supplied by adjacency lists and k in unary. Computation is deterministic on a multitape Turing machine, including the time to write the binary numerator and denominator of F. There must be one algorithm and one polynomial time bound valid for all inputs. The constants c and C do not depend on G or k. The algorithm may inspect the whole graph, but may not use a cover-time oracle. This computational target is an editorial replacement of the source’s unrestricted request for a characterization: it makes admissibility decidable at the level of a proposed algorithm and theorem, but does not require a closed-form graph invariant. A characterization requiring exponential computation does not satisfy this selected variant.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction, polynomial bit-complexity bound, and both uniform approximation inequalities, or a complete Lean-checked proof that no such deterministic polynomial-time approximation exists. A conditional computational lower bound must identify its assumption and is only a conditional answer. Exact computation by an exponentially large product-state chain is insufficient.
context:
Rivera, Sauerwald and Sylvester explicitly distinguish worst-case starting tuples from independent stationary starts. They introduce partial mixing times and derive useful bounds and characterizations on several graph families.

The source asks broadly for a general worst-start characterization. The present card deliberately selects a computational version: a deterministic polynomial-time constant-factor evaluation. This added efficiency requirement is an editorial choice, not a quoted conjecture of the authors.
why: A graph-general cover-time law would quantify the speedup obtainable from parallel random exploration.

import_provenance.original_title: A general characterization of parallel random-walk cover time
import_provenance.original_statement: For any connected undirected graph G and k independent lazy random walks with worst-case starting vertices, characterize within constant factors the expected time until their union has visited every vertex. The challenge is a graph-general analogue of single-walk cover-time theory, including the speedup as k varies.

sentences: Several independent lazy walks explore the same connected graph in parallel.
The target quantity is expected time until their combined visits cover every vertex, maximized over starting tuples.
Stationary starts and a forced common starting point are different conventions.
The source provides partial-mixing comparisons and sharp results for several graph families.
The selected editorial variant requires a deterministic polynomial-time constant-factor evaluator with the walk count encoded in unary.
